title: My Journey Building Projects with ESP32: Lessons, Challenges, and IoT Development Insights
excerpt: Why I chose the ESP32 for my embedded systems projects, common beginner mistakes, and insights on moving from prototypes to professional IoT applications.
content:
## Introduction: Why I Chose ESP32 for Embedded Systems Projects

![ESP32 Dev Board](/images/esp32_hero_banner.jpg)

When I started working with embedded systems, I discovered that choosing the right microcontroller can completely change the possibilities of a project. Among the different development boards available, the ESP32 became one of my preferred choices because of its powerful features, especially its built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities.

Unlike traditional microcontrollers such as the Arduino Uno, which has limited processing power, memory, and connectivity options, the ESP32 provides the flexibility needed for modern IoT applications. It allows developers to create connected systems, web dashboards, remote monitoring platforms, and intelligent automation solutions.

My experience with the ESP32 has mainly been through practical projects, especially my dual-axis solar tracker, where I needed a microcontroller capable of handling sensors, motors, data processing, and internet communication simultaneously.

## What Makes the ESP32 Different from Other Microcontrollers?

The ESP32 is a powerful microcontroller developed for embedded and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. One of its biggest advantages is the integration of wireless communication directly on the board.

For me, the main reason I prefer the ESP32 is its built-in:

- Wi-Fi module
- Bluetooth capability
- Higher number of GPIO pins
- Dual-core processing capability
- Better support for IoT applications

Compared with the Arduino Uno, the ESP32 offers more possibilities because the Arduino Uno is more limited in terms of processing power, memory, and available pins.

I have not personally worked with the ESP8266 enough to make a detailed comparison, but from my experience, the ESP32 already provides everything needed for advanced IoT projects.

## My First ESP32 Project: A Dual-Axis Solar Tracker

![Dual-Axis Solar Tracker Prototype](/images/solar_tracker_project.jpg)

The first major project I built using an ESP32 was a dual-axis solar tracker.

The reason I selected the ESP32 was not only because of its processing capability but mainly because I wanted to create a complete monitoring system around the solar tracker.

The objective was to allow users to:

- Monitor the position of the solar panel
- Track the movement angle
- Know the direction of movement
- Monitor energy production
- Analyze energy generation over time through graphs

To achieve this, I needed a microcontroller capable of communicating with a dashboard through Wi-Fi.

The ESP32 was the ideal choice because it provides more GPIO pins than an Arduino Uno and has a dual-core processor. This opened the possibility of separating tasks, where one processing core could handle hardware operations while another could manage communication tasks such as Wi-Fi connectivity.

This project taught me that selecting a microcontroller should always depend on the final application requirements, not just the availability of the board.

## Common ESP32 Mistakes Beginners Should Avoid

One of the biggest challenges I discovered when working with ESP32 is understanding the pin configuration.

Many beginners start using the board without carefully studying the pin allocation. Different ESP32 development boards may have different layouts, and confusing one pin with another can create serious problems.

For example, on some ESP32 boards, the CMD pin can easily be confused with the ground connection because of its position near the power pins. A wrong connection can cause the entire project to malfunction, leading developers to search for software problems when the issue is actually wiring.

Another important challenge is the ESP32 analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The ADC readings are not always perfectly stable, meaning calibration is often required, especially when working with sensors.

Power stability is also very important. If the ground connection is unstable, sensor readings can become unreliable.

Other common problems include:

- Poor project planning
- Using damaged jumper wires
- Not testing components individually
- Not checking hardware connections carefully

Sometimes a simple broken wire internally can waste hours of troubleshooting because the damage is not visible.

## My Favorite ESP32 Feature: Built-In Wi-Fi

The most useful ESP32 feature for me is the built-in Wi-Fi capability.

The reason is simple: the ESP32 can communicate directly with other devices without requiring additional communication modules.

It can operate as:

- A Wi-Fi client
- A web server
- A communication device inside an IoT network

For example, during my projects, I can connect my computer to the same network as the ESP32 and communicate directly with the board.

This makes it possible to create dashboards, monitoring systems, and remote-control applications without adding extra hardware.

Although Bluetooth is an interesting feature, I have not yet used it for a major project. Most of my applications have focused on Wi-Fi-based communication.

## Challenges I Faced Programming the ESP32

One of the biggest difficulties I experienced was uploading programs to the ESP32.

Sometimes everything would compile correctly, but during the final upload stage, the process would fail.

The solution I discovered was related to the boot process:

When the serial monitor displays the connection message, pressing and holding the boot button allows the upload process to start successfully.

Another challenge was working with the Arduino IDE. Installing and managing ESP32 board packages was sometimes difficult.

To improve my workflow, I started using PlatformIO with MicroPython-related workflows and command-line upload methods. Using the upload commands gave me better control over the development process.

This experience taught me that understanding development tools is just as important as understanding the hardware itself.

## Components I Commonly Use with ESP32

![ESP32 Wired to LCD Display](/images/esp32_lcd_display.jpg)

In my projects, one of the components I use most frequently with ESP32 is the LCD display with an I2C interface.

The reason is practical: most embedded systems need a way to display information locally.

An LCD allows users to see:

- Sensor measurements
- System status
- Operating modes
- Calculated values

I have also worked with OLED displays and different sensors, but LCD displays remain one of the most common components in my ESP32 projects because they are simple, reliable, and easy to integrate.

## My ESP32 Project Development Workflow

When starting a new ESP32 project, my first step is understanding the required functionality.

My workflow is:

1.  **Understand the Application**: Before selecting components, I define what the system should achieve.
2.  **Select Components**: Sensors and modules are chosen based on the application requirements.
3.  **Develop the Program**: I design the software structure before connecting all hardware components.
4.  **Assemble and Test**: After programming, I connect the hardware and begin testing.
5.  **Calibration and Optimization**: Sensors and systems are calibrated to improve accuracy.
6.  **Documentation**: Finally, I document the complete process so another person can reproduce the project.

Documentation is important because engineering projects should not depend on only one person's knowledge.

## How I Recommend Learning ESP32 From Scratch

For beginners, the first step is understanding what the ESP32 is and why it is different from other microcontrollers.

Before building advanced projects, learn:

- ESP32 architecture
- GPIO control
- Digital input and output
- Basic programming concepts

Start with simple projects, even something as basic as blinking an LED.

Although using an ESP32 for an LED project may seem excessive, the goal is not the project itself—the goal is understanding the system.

One important recommendation I give beginners is:

**Do not blindly copy and paste code.**

Even if you use someone else's example, rewrite the code manually. Type every line yourself and understand what each instruction does.

This helps you become familiar with:

- Programming syntax
- Functions
- Digital communication
- Microcontroller behavior

Learning by typing and analyzing code creates a stronger connection with the system.

## Moving From Beginner Projects to Professional IoT Systems

After mastering the basics, developers should explore the communication advantages of the ESP32.

Important areas include:

- Wi-Fi communication
- Serial communication
- I2C communication
- USB communication
- Cloud connectivity
- Real-time monitoring

The ESP32 becomes much more powerful when combined with networking technologies because it can transform a simple electronic circuit into a connected IoT system.

The combination of its small size, communication capabilities, and dual-core processing makes it suitable for professional applications.

## Using ESP32 for Commercial Products

One important advantage of the ESP32 ecosystem is that the same programming concepts used in beginner projects can often be transferred to professional modules.

A developer can start with a development board and later move to a commercial ESP32-based product.

The main changes usually involve:

- Adjusting GPIO assignments
- Understanding the new hardware layout
- Optimizing the design for production

The software foundation can remain similar.

This makes the ESP32 a valuable platform for moving from prototypes to real products.

## Final Thoughts

My journey with the ESP32 has shown me that successful embedded systems development is not only about choosing powerful hardware. It is about understanding the system, planning properly, testing carefully, and learning from problems.

The ESP32 is more than a microcontroller. It is a complete platform for developing modern IoT solutions.

Whether building a simple sensor project, a smart home device, or an industrial monitoring system, the ESP32 provides the flexibility and capability needed to turn ideas into real-world applications.

The most important lesson I have learned is:

**Understand the technology you use. Do not just make a project work—understand why it works.**
